deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no derivations, formulas or computations. It is a handwritten lecture announcement (Vorlesungsankündigung) signed 'B. Riemann' for the Winter Semester 1858/59 at Göttingen. It lists three courses:

(1) 'Integration der partiellen Differentialgleichungen mit Anwendungen auf physikalische Fragen' (integration of partial differential equations, with applications to physical questions), Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 12-1.

(2) 'Theoretische Physik, insbesondere Theorie der Elasticität und mechanische Wärmetheorie' (theoretical physics, especially the theory of elasticity and the mechanical theory of heat), same weekdays, 9-10, beginning 1 November.

(3) 'Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Größe, insbesondere über hypergeometrische Reihen und verwandte Transcendenten' (functions of one complex variable, especially hypergeometric series and related transcendental functions), same days, 4-5. The start date was corrected; apparently 'Nov' was struck and replaced by 'October', i.e. beginning 26 October.

Context:
- Course 1 belongs to the PDE lecture cycle later edited by K. Hattendorff as 'Partielle Differentialgleichungen und deren Anwendung auf physikalische Fragen' (1869).
- Course 3 continues Riemann's 1857 work: the paper on Gauss's series F(α,β,γ,x), which introduced the P-function and monodromy viewpoint, and the Abelian functions paper.
- Course 2 reflects his teaching of mathematical physics. The mechanical theory of heat was then current (Clausius, 1850s).

The page is an administrative document. Its value is biographical and chronological: dates, hours and course titles of Riemann's teaching.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative lecture announcement with no mathematical content. Riemann's teaching on PDEs and on hypergeometric functions in this period is well documented, including in published lecture lists and the Hattendorff edition. The only minor interest is the exact schedule and the physics course title (elasticity and mechanical heat theory).
transcription_corrections: In item 3, the start date reads 'Anfang d. 26 [Nov struck] October'. Only 'Nov' appears to be struck; '26' seems to be retained, so the intended date is 26 October. Writing '[-26 Nov-]' as fully deleted is probably inaccurate.
The initial 'Über' in item 3 is indeed struck through, which is consistent with the given transcription.
Weekday abbreviations: the image reads approximately 'Mon. Dinst. Donn. u. Freit.', i.e. Montag, Dienstag, Donnerstag, Freitag. The expansion in the transcription is fine.
A folio number '41' is visible in the upper right margin and is not included in the transcription.
